cohort: The study included 36,835 pregnancies of women diagnosed with chronic medical conditions before pregnancy and a reference group of 1,084,623 pregnancies of women without known chronic medical conditions, utilizing data from the Netherlands Perinatal Registry.
finding: Women with chronic medical conditions are significantly more likely to experience preterm birth, caesarean births, and NICU admission of the new-born compared to women without such conditions.
mod_finding: Spontaneous birth was significantly lower, while assisted vaginal birth, planned caesarean birth, and emergency caesarean birth were significantly higher in women with chronic medical conditions across all subgroups compared to the reference group.
